title: 컴퓨터기반 협력학습(CSCL)에서 협력적 메타인지 지원이 집단과제수행 및 학습태도에 미치는 영향

abstracts.value:
컴퓨터기반 협력학습(CSCL)에서는 학습자들 각자 분담된 역할을 수행하면서, 집단인지체제를 이루어 협력적으로 문제를 해결하므로, 개별학습상황에서의 메타인지 지원과는 달리 메타인지도 학습자들간 협력적으로 수행될 수 있도록 지원되어야 한다. 학습효과 측정 또한 협력 학습상황이라는 것을 고려하여 집단과제수행을 측정대상으로 하여야 한다. 이에 본 연구에서는 CSCL에서 협력적 메타인지 지원이 집단과제수행과 학습태도에 어떠한 영향을 미치는지 알아보고자 했다.
이를 위해 2개반의 대학생 102명을 실험집단과 비교집단으로 설정하고, 실험집단은 협력적 메타인지가 지원되는 CSCL에서, 비교집단은 협력적 메타인지가 지원되지 않는 CSCL에서 집단 과제를 수행하였다. 실험 사전에 사전지식검사, 메타인지 검사, 학습태도 검사를 실시하였고, 사후에 동일한 학습태도 검사와 집단 과제수행 검사를 실시하였다.
실험집단과 비교집단의 집단과제수행 결과와 학습태도 결과를 비교해본 결과, 협력적 메타인지가 집단과제수행에 긍정적인 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났으나, 학습태도에는 영향을 미치지 않는 것으로 밝혀졌다.
차후 연구를 통하여, 개별 메타인지 지원 집단과 협력적 메타인지 지원 집단간의 집단과제수행을 비교해볼 필요가 있으며, 소집단 구성원간의 상호작용을 세밀하게 관찰할 필요가 있다.

Metacognition which can be developed through training has been regarded as one of the crucial factors in learning. Strategies to support metacognition have been studied to improve learning effect. if an instructor or an instructional designer doesn't support metacognitive activities, learners don't use metacognition by themselves. Therefore, development and training of the metacognitive strategies are required.
In CSCL(Computer Supported Collaborative Learning), each student plays a role while solving a problem collaboratively as a unit group cognitive system. Metacognitive process for group cognition should be performed collaboratively among students in CSCL. Also, learning effect may be measured by task performance of a unit group. The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of the collaborative metacognition support on the task performance of a group and learning attitude in CSCL.
The subjects of this study were randomly assigned to one of the two groups to test the effects of the selected treatment variables. Each group was provided with two programs which were collaborative metacognition support and non-CMS.
The major research findings of the study were as follows:
First, the grade of the task performance of the group which was supported in collaborative metacognition was significantly higher than that of other group(F=5.10, p<.05). That is, it can be concluded that support of collaborative metacognition has influenced task performance of group positively.
Second, There was not a significant difference in groups' task performances between CMS and non-CMS in CSCL(F=0.25, p>.05). That result may be resulted from to composing by small members of students groups and unexpectedly competing for good grades among groups or students
For elaborating more sophisticated relationships among the variables, it is necessary for futther studies to compare with individual metacognition support and collaborative metacognition support and to observe interaction closely among members in small group.
